event.title: Amnesty Report Alleges Moroccan Surveillance of Journalists and Activists
event.canonical_title: Amnesty Report Alleges Moroccan Surveillance of Journalists and Activists
event.summary: A recent report by Amnesty International claims that Moroccan intelligence employs extensive surveillance tactics, including spyware and hidden microphones, to monitor and silence journalists, activists, and rights defenders. The findings suggest a systematic effort to suppress critical voices in the country.

timeline.title: Turkish Authorities Raid Halk TV, Appoint Trustee Amid Media Freedom Concerns
timeline.summary: On October 14, Turkish police conducted a raid on the headquarters of Halk TV in Istanbul, surrounding the building with barricades. The authorities appointed a trustee to take control of the independent broadcaster's operations, leading to widespread outrage regarding media freedom in the country.
key_facts: Turkish police raided Halk TV's headquarters in Istanbul.
Police barricades were set up around the building.
A trustee was appointed to take control of Halk TV's operations.

event_overview.title: About Media Freedom
event_overview.subject: Media Freedom
event_overview.summary: Media freedom is the ongoing human-rights and governance issue concerning whether journalists, media outlets and the public can seek, receive and impart information without unlawful interference, intimidation or censorship. It encompasses legal protections for expression and press independence as well as practical concerns such as surveillance, safety, ownership and state action affecting news organizations.

facts.label: International legal basis
facts.value: Article 19 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights, adopted on December 10, 1948, recognizes the freedom to seek, receive and impart information and ideas through any media and across frontiers; the ICCPR was adopted on December 16, 1966 and entered into force on March 23, 1976.

facts.label: Protected activity
facts.value: Under the UN Human Rights Committee’s interpretation of ICCPR Article 19, the protection covers journalism, political discourse and public-affairs commentary, as well as the means used to disseminate them, including newspapers and other media.

facts.label: Limits and safeguards
facts.value: Freedom of opinion under the ICCPR may not be restricted. Restrictions on expression are permitted only when prescribed by law and necessary for specified aims, including protecting others’ rights or reputations, national security, public order, public health or morals; UN guidance further frames the test in terms of necessity and proportionality.

facts.label: Relevant treaty commitments
facts.value: Morocco ratified the ICCPR on May 3, 1979, and Türkiye ratified it on September 23, 2003. Türkiye also ratified the European Convention on Human Rights on May 18, 1954; Article 10 of that convention covers freedom of expression and the press.

facts.label: Journalist safety framework
facts.value: UNESCO’s UN Plan of Action on the Safety of Journalists and the Issue of Impunity was endorsed in 2012. It is a multi-stakeholder framework focused on prevention, protection and prosecution, reflecting that physical, legal and digital threats to journalists can affect media freedom.

event_overview.scope_note: This timeline follows selected developments concerning alleged surveillance in Morocco and state action affecting a Turkish broadcaster; it does not attempt to measure or catalogue all media-freedom conditions, court cases or incidents worldwide.
